title: `is_action_just_pressed_by_event` and `is_action_just_released_by_event` always return `false` when triggered by mouse button clicks
body:
### Tested versions

4.6.2-stable

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable (5e984564c) - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 61.61 GiB memory

### Issue description

I want to know if the action was triggered by this specific event that I receive in `_unhandled_input`. However, when the action is triggered by a mouse click, `is_action_just_pressed_by_event` and `is_action_just_released_by_event` will always return `false`, even though they originally triggered the action.

I debugged this a week ago, the issue comes from the fact that for mouse input Godot internally does some conversion, which results in a new input object creation, hence `is_action_just_pressed_by_event` and `is_action_just_released_by_event` fail to match the original event's id to the converted id. I think it was the `xformed_by` that was doing this.

I'd assume this is a bug, because there is no way to tell if the mouse click triggered the action. If it's not a bug, then `is_action_just_pressed_by_event` and `is_action_just_released_by_event` are not very useful, and cannot be used universally, because they act differently for keyboard and mouse inputs.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Map an input action to a left mouse click
2. Catch input event in `_unhandled_input`
3. Check `is_action_just_pressed_by_event` and `is_action_just_released_by_event` are `false`

N/A
